title: Aug 28 Results: The Bayesian Truth in 73.3%

## Model Validation: A Strong 11-4 Performance

Our predictive model posted an impressive 11-4 record on August 28, achieving 73.3% accuracy across fifteen matchups. What's particularly notable from a statistical inference perspective is that our model's confidence levels correlated strongly with actual outcomes—a key indicator of calibration quality that separates signal from noise in probabilistic forecasting.

## The Distribution of Confidence and Outcomes

Examining our probability bands reveals instructive patterns. Picks with 60%+ confidence went 7-1 (87.5%), while our lower-confidence selections (52-59%) posted a respectable 4-3 mark. This differential suggests our underlying regression model is correctly weighting key variables—run differential, park factors, bullpen leverage metrics, and recent team performance indicators.

## Decomposing the Misses: When Base Rates Mislead

Our two losses merit deeper examination. The Cubs-Reds miss (61% confidence) likely reflects the inherent volatility in divisional matchups where familiarity reduces our information advantage. The Marlins-Nationals error (60% confidence) occurred in a context where recent-form indicators may have overweighted Miami's small-sample surge.

This is precisely where Bayesian thinking matters: we update priors based on new evidence, but must remain skeptical of recency bias in a sport where true-talent estimations require larger sample sizes than late-season hot streaks provide.

## The High-Confidence Cluster: 63% Picks Go 3-0

Our three highest-confidence selections—Dodgers (63%), Blue Jays (63%), and Brewers (63%)—all converted successfully. This perfect 3-0 mark at our top probability threshold validates the model's ability to identify matchups where multiple factors align: starting pitcher quality measured by FIP and xFIP, lineup depth via wRC+, and bullpen reliability through leverage-adjusted metrics.

The Dodgers-Tigers outcome particularly exemplified this convergence: LA's superior team WAR, Detroit's negative run differential, and a significant park-adjusted offensive advantage all contributed to what the model correctly identified as a high-probability scenario.

## No Games Tomorrow: A Moment for Recalibration

With no MLB games scheduled for August 29, this presents an optimal opportunity to refine our regression parameters. We'll be running cross-validation tests on our recent predictions, examining whether adjustments to our rest-day factors or late-season fatigue coefficients might improve model fit.

In the meantime, today's 73.3% accuracy reinforces confidence in our methodological framework while reminding us that probabilistic forecasting isn't about perfection—it's about long-run edge and proper calibration of uncertainty.
